variants.name: Downloaded script or library passed to existing interpreter/loader

variants.name: Stream download directly into interpreter or process substitution

variants.name: Compile/link native program in home, then execute output

variants.name: Removed image/container restarted through old name, daemon state, API or retained layers
variants.previous_reason: U04: a recorded live holder and forked child are both observed, then both absent before successful removal. Former entry, retained image archive and name/start requests refuse; removing the image also verifies. [Round-4 evidence](SELFTEST.md).
variants.v4_implication: Removal must account for remaining installed image/package content as well as live descendants and executable authority; establish whether retained archive bytes are material before calling them exempt.

variants.name: Documented privileged package/service/account/network/firewall administration
variants.previous_reason: R01/R04/R05/R08: ordinary authority is restricted to declaration tools; direct account/package/service/network/Bluetooth/firewall clients, daemon APIs and native nft library mutation refuse. Host-held external operator root is outside this grant, as specified by BC1. [Round-1 evidence](SELFTEST.md).
variants.v4_implication: Test actual superuser invocations of built-in tools: changing guards/rights through those tools must record/apply. A limited sudo grant or inaccessible backend alone is insufficient. Direct root mutation outside them is breaking and is not required to be blocked.

variants.name: Built-in privileged tool changes guards, permissions, mounts or execution policy
variants.previous_reason: R01/R09: no generic sudo shell, environment launcher or mount tool is granted; guard-changing backends are private and authority-bearing declaration injections refuse. The external operator can still deliberately break mechanisms. [Round-1 evidence](SELFTEST.md).
variants.v4_implication: Test actual superuser invocations of built-in tools: changing guards/rights through those tools must record/apply. A limited sudo grant or inaccessible backend alone is insufficient. Direct root mutation outside them is breaking and is not required to be blocked.

variants.name: Retained arbitrary privileged hooks and multi-resource live side effects
variants.previous_reason: R09/R12: arbitrary privileged hooks are refused and one live service mismatch restores the prior declaration. General multi-resource side-effect restoration, especially across daemon/device state, is not established. [Round-1 evidence](SELFTEST.md).
variants.v4_implication: Effects of supported installation hooks still belong to built-in transactions, including root; distinguish direct superuser bypass outside the built-in tools. Multi-resource/device readback and restoration remain unproved.

variants.name: Root editor with documented package installer
variants.previous_reason: B: Stricter target treats an editor installer as built-in under root. ed has no such installer, but arbitrary editor installation is not mediated fully.
variants.v4_implication: The embedded installer part is explicitly an installer, even in a general-purpose editor. Demonstrate its declaration-writing behavior under root; direct root editing outside that part is breaking. The old role ambiguity is not carried as a decision.

variants.name: All C1–C10: partial activation failure, stalled worker, or no report at one hour
variants.previous_reason: T01–T03 exercise ten failures, two worker stalls and supervisor death. Recovery can itself stall or fail; the total deadline is recorded but complete restoration by one hour is not enforced for every effect. This is a supervisor/backend limitation. [Round-3 evidence](SELFTEST.md).
variants.v4_implication: Recovery remains a carried engineering obligation. The explicit one-hour deadline is historical implementation/test policy, not a v4 sentence; evaluate P1/P2 against the last successful declaration and do not invent a deadline rule.
